_comment: DOOM's sounds go through the game's own UI bank: the game creates its UI sound events once at startup
from five fixed banks and never loads a mod's bank, so tools/patch_bank.py swaps samples INSIDE
content/sfx/gui.bank for DOOM's, and the host asks for the GUI event type that plays them.
The effects live on gui_navigation and the music on gui_garage, and that separation is the point.
One FMOD event holds a small pool of instances and steals the oldest when it fills; the music is a
103 s instance, so it is permanently the oldest thing in its pool. While the effects shared the
garage event with it, DOOM's gunfire evicted the music within a frame or two -- audible effects,
silent music, which is exactly what the game did (proven by snippets/musicburst.js, 2026-09-17).
gui_navigation has NINE parameters; the stock gui_events.table maps only 0-4. Params 5-8 are reached
by claiming four types the stock table leaves unmapped, which is what `claims` below does through
tools/build_table.py. Nothing the game plays for itself changes: params 0-4 keep their menu clicks
and the garage slots go back to stock, apart from the pneumatic one that carries E1M1.

slots._role: weapons fire; the shotgun shares this now that there are four slots, not six
deaths and pain grunts, merged for the same reason
explosions (barrels and rockets only; imp fireball impacts stay silent, they misled as explosions)

pickups. GUI_WARNING is param 1 and needs no claim -- the stock table already maps it -- so this costs the game's warning sound and nothing else. itemup is DOOM's blip for health, armour and ammo, and it peaks at 15% of full scale where the gunfire peaks at 100%: at its own level it was inaudible in game at 0.202 s AND at 0.550 s, so length was never the problem. normalize brings it to 90% peak, from the 44.1 kHz 16-bit source so the gain does not amplify 8-bit quantisation noise

musicSwaps._note: GUI_PART_APPLY plays the pneumatic sample; it plays a full 103 s track (unlike the menu-click slots). Host fires GUI_PART_APPLY when a DOOM level starts, loops every 103 s. Pickup sound sacrificed for music.

_musicExperiment: EXPERIMENT: every UI music track is DOOM E1M1, so any menu/gameplay music is unmistakable and GUI_MUSIC_MENU/GAMEPLAY/END are deterministic. If it works, the real version uses different DOOM tracks (E1M1-E1M9) for variety.
_note: 5 effect groups + music. gui_navigation stops at param 8: params 5-8 are claimed through the table override, and GUI_WARNING (param 1) is borrowed from the stock five. The shotgun still shares the weapons slot and pain shares deaths; params 0, 2, 3 and 4 are four more stock clicks that could be borrowed to unmerge them, one menu sound each.
